S15.01.note: The name is computed by getShortDisplayName, so there is no literal visible string for it in the code.
steps: Open the app and go to a new chat.
Look at the bottom bar of the message box, next to the + button.
Read the model name on that button.
Send a short message and compare the name on the button with the model shown under the answer (see S15.32).
S15.01.where: Chat screen > composer bar: the model name button beside the + (Add to chat) button

S15.02.note: For providers with a logo, the row shows the logo icon and no provider text; the provider name text appears only for providers without a logo. The text itself is built from the provider name in service.ts.
steps: Tap the model name in the composer bar.
In the Models sheet, look at the small grey text to the right of each model name.
Compare the text with the company or provider shown for that model.
S15.02.where: Chat screen > tap the model name in the composer > Models sheet > any model row

S15.03.note: The chevron has no visible words; its accessibility label is 'More <line name> models'.
steps: Tap the model name in the composer bar.
Scroll the Models sheet to a model row that has a chevron on its right.
Tap the chevron to open the other models in that line.
Check that the related versions of one model line appear together under that row.
S15.03.where: Chat screen > tap the model name in the composer > Models sheet > open a model row's chevron (More models)

steps: Tap the model name in the composer bar.
Tap the field that says Search models….
Type part of a model name, such as a few letters.
Check that the list shrinks to the models whose names match.
S15.04.where: Chat screen > tap the model name in the composer > Models sheet > Search models…

S15.05.note: Long-press on a model that needs sign-in or an upgrade opens the upgrade path instead of favouriting.
steps: Tap the model name in the composer bar.
Press and hold a model row for about half a second.
Check that a small gold star appears on that row.
Scroll to the top of the Models sheet and check that the starred model is in the Favorites group.
S15.05.where: Chat screen > tap the model name in the composer > Models sheet > long-press a model row

steps: Pick any model from the Models sheet so the sheet closes.
Tap the model name in the composer bar again.
Look at the group titled Recent at the top of the list.
Check that the model you just used is listed there.
S15.06.where: Chat screen > tap the model name in the composer > Models sheet > Recent group at the top

S15.08.note: Auto rows are built from the routing profiles in apps/mobile/lib/models.ts; the other profile names in that file are Instant, Best and Economy.
steps: Tap the model name in the composer bar.
Look at the rows at the top of the Models sheet, above Recent.
Tap the row named Auto and wait for the sheet to close.
Send a message and check the model shown under the answer (see S15.32) to see which model the product picked.
S15.08.where: Chat screen > tap the model name in the composer > Models sheet > top row labelled Auto

steps: Tap the model name in the composer bar.
Tap a model row that has no lock icon.
Check that the sheet closes and the composer shows the new name.
Send a message and check the model shown under the answer (see S15.32).
S15.10.where: Chat screen > tap the model name in the composer > Models sheet > tap a model row

S15.16.note: The chip only filters to fast-speed models; the code has no visible text that says models are faster or slower. The Speed section with the Fast switch only states that fast answers cost more usage.
steps: Open the side menu and tap AGI Cloud in the mode switch.
Tap the model name in the composer bar.
Tap the chip labelled Instant under the search field.
Check that only the quick models remain in the list.
S15.16.where: Chat screen > side menu > AGI Cloud (mode switch) > tap the model name in the composer > Instant chip in the Models sheet

S15.18.note: The badge reads Upgrade or Not included depending on whether purchases are available. The plan name (for example Max) appears only in the row's accessibility hint, not as visible text.
steps: Tap the model name in the composer bar.
Find a model row with a lock icon and a yellow badge.
Read the badge text and compare it with Expected.
Tap that row and check that the upgrade options open.
S15.18.where: Chat screen > tap the model name in the composer > Models sheet > a model row with a lock icon and an Upgrade badge

S15.21.needs: a live provider outage (cannot be made on demand) or an on-device model that is not on this device
S15.21.note: The badge appears only when the server reports an outage, so a tester cannot force it. The visible line under the row says Unavailable right now. Try again soon or pick another model.
steps: Tap the model name in the composer bar.
Look for a row with a grey Unavailable badge and a dimmed look.
Tap the row and check that nothing changes and the model is not selected.
S15.21.where: Chat screen > tap the model name in the composer > Models sheet > a model row with an Unavailable badge

S15.22.needs: a signed-in AGI Cloud account and a reasoning model
S15.22.note: The button is hidden for models without reasoning, so the tester must choose a reasoning model first.
steps: Open the side menu and tap AGI Cloud, then open a new chat.
Choose a model that thinks (reasoning model) from the Models sheet.
Tap the effort button in the composer bar.
Move the effort slider to another level, then tap Done.
Check that the effort name changes on the slider and in the composer.
S15.22.where: Chat screen > composer bar > reasoning effort button (appears for a reasoning model in AGI Cloud mode)

S15.24.note: The styles are Normal, Concise, Explanatory, Learning and Formal, with the description Short, direct answers for Concise. There is no explicit longer-answer option, so the length preference is only a style.
steps: Tap the + button in the composer bar (labelled Add to chat).
Tap Choose style.
Pick Concise, Normal, Explanatory, Learning or Formal.
Send the same question twice, once with Concise and once with Explanatory, and compare the answer lengths.
S15.24.where: Chat screen > + (Add to chat) > Choose style

S15.27.needs: a device with room for an on-device model (downloading is required for Ready)
S15.27.note: The On device group title is in ModelPickerSheet.tsx. The Local Mode label is the switch's accessibility label.
steps: Open the side menu and tap Local Mode in the mode switch.
Tap the model name in the composer bar.
Look for the group titled On device and a row with a chip icon.
Download a model if needed (Download badge), wait until it shows Ready, then pick it and check the composer name.
S15.27.where: Side menu > Local Mode (mode switch) > tap the model name in the composer > Models sheet > On device group

S15.29.note: The choice is stored under the model-store key in apps/mobile/src/features/model-picker/store.ts.
steps: Pick a model from the Models sheet.
Close the app completely and open it again.
Go to a new chat and read the model name in the composer bar.
Check that it is the model you picked before closing.
S15.29.where: Chat screen > tap the model name in the composer > Models sheet > pick a model, then close and reopen the app

S15.30.note: Selecting a model in an existing chat is saved for that conversation through setConversationModel in app/(app)/chat/[id].tsx.
steps: Open chat A and pick model X from the Models sheet.
Start a new chat and check its composer model name differs or stays as the default.
Go back to chat A and check the composer still shows model X.
Check that a different chat with no change still shows its own model.
S15.30.where: Open an existing chat > tap the model name in the composer > Models sheet > pick a model

S15.32.needs: a signed-in AGI Cloud account for the AGI Cloud label
S15.32.note: The footer is built in ProvenanceFooter.tsx; it is hidden while the answer is still streaming. An Auto answer shows the model as Auto.
steps: Send a message in a chat and wait for the answer to finish streaming.
Look at the small text line under the answer.
Read the text, which joins the provider and the model name with a dot.
Compare it with the model you picked in the composer.
S15.32.where: Chat screen > under any finished assistant answer, the small line with provider and model
